rubric_scores.why: The rep started pitching with no agenda.

rubric_scores.evidence_quote: What's the biggest challenge with time tracking right now?
rubric_scores.why: The rep asked about problems once and moved on after the first answer.
Nobody discussed what the problem costs.
The rep never asked how the decision gets made.
The rep played the situation back in the prospect's words and checked it.

rubric_scores.evidence_quote: let me walk you through the platform
rubric_scores.why: The rep delivered a long feature list with no link to the prospect's problems.

rubric_scores.evidence_quote: We're actually cheaper than most of the market.
rubric_scores.why: The rep got defensive and argued with the objection.

rubric_scores.evidence_quote: if you sign this month I can take twenty percent off
rubric_scores.why: The rep offered a discount before the prospect pushed back at all.
A specific meeting with a day, time, and attendees was agreed on the call.

rapport.why: The rep opened with a specific, personal question.

tone_match.why: The rep's pace and wording tracked the prospect's.

price_handling.evidence_quote: if you sign this month I can take twenty percent off
price_handling.why: The rep offered a discount before the prospect pushed back at all.

objections.evidence_quote: Can you just send me some info and I'll look it over?
objections.why: The rep argued instead of asking what the prospect needed.

top_misses: No upfront agreement on what the call would cover or decide.
Never got the prospect to put a number on the cost of doing nothing.
Left without a measurable goal to anchor the value.

rewrite.original_quote: let me walk you through the platform
rewrite.better_version: You said our payroll coordinator spends a full day at every month end on tracking technician hours. Here is the one part of the product that fixes that.

one_thing_to_change: Open every call with a three-part agenda and ask the prospect what they would add.
